A1.justification: Both complete 47-page PDFs describe the same M3-Agent and M3-Bench work. Text and visual comparison covers the main paper and Appendices A–H; differences are confined to dataset counts and first-page date/version text.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations and ablations in Tables 5–7, memorization evaluations in Appendix E, and human and synthetic-data quality assessments in Appendices A and D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark accuracies, ablations, appendix memorization evaluations, and annotation-quality assessments.

M1.justification: The memorization/control architecture, entity-centric memory graph, retrieval procedures, imitation learning, and DAPO training remain identical, including Algorithms 1–2 and appendix implementation procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions retain M3-Bench-robot, M3-Bench-web, VideoMME-long, the same training-data sources, and the same question types and scenarios. The revised sample counts do not document a change in task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Table 5 retains the same Socratic-model variants, MovieChat, MA-LMM, Flash-VStream, Gemini-Agent, and Gemini-GPT4o-Hybrid. Comparator membership in the ablation and appendix memorization evaluations is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported M3-Bench-web size changes from 929 videos and 5,037 QA pairs to 920 videos and 3,214 QA pairs in the introduction and Table 2—a substantial 36% reduction in reported QA count. The introduction also changes robot QA pairs from 1,344 to 1,276, matching Table 2 in both versions. Other protocols remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether these are reporting corrections or actual evaluation-set changes.

E4.justification: The memory-component, control-model, model-size, and prompting ablations in Tables 6–7 are unchanged. Appendix checkpoint evaluations, training curves, quality analyses, and case studies are also identical.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting and sampling descriptions are unchanged, including the 100-example evaluator-agreement assessment in Section 3.3. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: All reported evaluation outcomes remain identical, including M3-Agent's Table 5 accuracies of 30.7, 48.9, and 61.8, the ablations, and Appendix Table 13. The changed dataset inventory counts do not establish new performance results or rerun experiments.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, reward and advantage definitions, algorithms, and appendix GRPO formulation are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the multimodal long-term-memory agent, M3-Bench, and claimed advantages of reinforcement-learning-based reasoning. Revised dataset totals do not alter these claims' substantive meaning or task scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of memory and reasoning benefits are unchanged. Section 5.5 and the conclusion retain the same limitations concerning fine-grained detail retention and spatial reasoning, without explaining the revised dataset totals.

D1.justification: Implementation details, preprocessing instructions, retrieval thresholds, hardware, hyperparameters, prompt templates, and code/data access statements are unchanged. No filtering or reproduction instructions accompany the revised dataset counts.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, bibliography, and positioning relative to memory-based agents and online video-understanding methods are identical.

P1.justification: The first-page date and arXiv version text are updated. Apart from numerical substitutions, the prose, terminology, section ordering, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, captions, table structures, and page layouts are unchanged. Table 2 changes only numerical cells; there are no added, removed, redrawn, or relocated displays.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves the robot-QA discrepancy between the introduction and Table 2 by reporting 1,276 consistently. However, 3,214 web QA pairs across 920 videos no longer reconcile with Section 3.2's unchanged requirement of at least five pairs per video. Neither the main text nor Appendix B explains filtering or the count revisions. This consistency gain and new reporting ambiguity prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
